Most AI code review tools just add more comments to your pull request. But more comments was never the goal.

results.title: LiveReview Review 2026: Risk-Scored AI Code Review & Pricing
results.content:
## Weaknesses

 Not open source in the OSI sense: the Sustainable Use License restricts commercial redistribution and competing services
 Newly generally available, and its outcome claims lean on Meta's RADAR results rather than published LiveReview data
 The incident-trained model only helps if the team records incidents and reverts
 SSO, local models and supported self-hosting at scale require a sales-quoted Enterprise plan, and there is no SOC 2 Type II certification
 The Free cloud plan caps teams at 3 members

## LiveReviewpricing

Free

$0

Billed monthly [...] The cloud Free plan is limited to 3 team members
 The 30-50% auto-approval figure is a vendor target, and the headline outcome numbers (50x fewer incidents, 3x fewer rollbacks) are Meta's reported RADAR results rather than LiveReview measurements
 The organization-specific risk model learns from reverts and incidents your team records, and the product pages do not say how much history it needs before its scores are reliable
 Hexmos states LiveReview is not SOC 2 Type II certified
 Repository Policies and running static analyzers such as Semgrep or ESLint alongside AI review are listed as coming soon
 Self-hosting needs Linux or macOS with Docker, bash and jq; the one-command demo mode is localhost-only without webhooks, and production use needs a reverse proxy setup [...] Not ideal for

Teams that need an OSI-licensed reviewer, organizations that require SOC 2 Type II from vendors, teams unwilling to let any pull request merge without a human approval, and teams that do not track incidents or reverts and so would not feed the risk model

Who it's for

Engineering managers, tech leads and platform teams responsible for review throughput and production stability, plus developers who want commit-time reviews in their terminal or editor
